description: Matches every element. Combine it with a scoped ancestor to keep broad rules within one component.

name: p
description: Matches elements by tag name. This rule styles every paragraph in its scope.

name: .card
description: Matches an element containing the named class token. An element can carry multiple classes.

name: #navigation
description: Matches the named ID. IDs should be unique within a document and contribute high specificity.

name: h1, h2, h3
description: Applies one rule to any selector in the comma-separated list. An invalid selector can invalidate an ordinary list.

name: .card p
description: Matches paragraphs at any depth inside a card, including paragraphs inside nested child elements.

name: .card > p
description: Matches paragraphs that are direct children of the card. Deeper descendants are excluded.

name: h2 + p
description: Matches a paragraph immediately after an h2 when both share a parent. Text nodes do not interrupt element adjacency.

name: h2 ~ p
description: Matches later sibling paragraphs after an h2 under the same parent; they need not be adjacent.

name: [disabled]
description: Matches an element with the attribute present, regardless of its value.

name: [type="email"]
description: Matches an attribute whose complete value equals the supplied string.

name: [class~="card"]
description: Matches a whole word in a whitespace-separated attribute value. It does not match part of a word.

name: [lang|="en"]
description: Matches an exact value or that value followed by a hyphen, such as en and en-US.

name: [href^="https://"]
description: Matches an attribute value that begins with the given string.

name: [href$=".pdf"]
description: Matches an attribute value ending in the given string. A query string after .pdf prevents this example from matching.

name: [data-label*="draft"]
description: Matches the given string anywhere inside the attribute value.

name: [data-state="open" i]
description: Uses the i flag for ASCII case-insensitive value matching. OPEN and open both match.

name: [data-state="open" s]
description: Uses the s flag to request case-sensitive value matching. Check support for this flag separately from basic attribute selectors.

name: :is(h1, h2, h3)
description: Matches any selector in its forgiving selector list. Its specificity comes from the most specific argument.

name: :where(h1, h2, h3)
description: Matches any selector in its forgiving selector list and contributes zero specificity, making overrides easier.

name: .card:not(.muted)
description: Matches cards that do not match the argument. Its specificity includes the most specific argument.

name: .card:has(> img)
description: Matches a card with a direct image child. Arguments describe relationships relative to the candidate element; this can style a parent based on its contents.

name: li:first-child
description: Matches a list item that is the first element child of its parent. It is not the first li if another element comes first.

name: li:last-child
description: Matches a list item that is the last element child of its parent.

name: p:only-child
description: Matches a paragraph when it is its parent’s only element child.

name: li:nth-child(2n + 1)
description: Matches list items at odd element-child positions. Counting starts at one and includes all element siblings.

name: :nth-child(2 of .card)
description: Matches the second sibling among those matching .card. The of selector filters the sibling set before counting.

name: li:nth-last-child(2)
description: Matches a list item at the second element-child position counted from the end.

name: p:first-of-type
description: Matches the first paragraph among sibling paragraphs, even when another element appears first.

support.notes: Before Edge 16, Microsoft Edge treats all unknown elements (such as custom elements) as the same element type.

name: p:last-of-type
description: Matches the last paragraph among sibling paragraphs.

support.notes: Before Edge 16, Microsoft Edge treats all unknown elements (such as custom elements) as the same element type.

name: p:nth-of-type(2n)
description: Matches paragraphs at even positions among sibling paragraphs. It counts tag names, not classes.

support.notes: Before Edge 16, Microsoft Edge treats all unknown elements (such as custom elements) as the same element type.

name: p:nth-last-of-type(2)
description: Matches the second paragraph counted backward among sibling paragraphs.

support.notes: Before Edge 16, Microsoft Edge treats all unknown elements (such as custom elements) as the same element type.

name: p:only-of-type
description: Matches a paragraph with no sibling paragraphs, even if siblings of other types exist.

support.notes: Before Edge 16, Microsoft Edge treats all unknown elements (such as custom elements) as the same element type.

name: .message:empty
description: Matches an element with no child elements or text content. Whitespace text can prevent matching in current implementations.

name: :root
description: Matches the document root, normally html in an HTML document. Useful for shared custom properties.

name: :scope > .card
description: Represents the current scoping root, such as the element used for a querySelector call. This selects its direct card children.

support.notes: Firefox 55 removes support for <style scoped> but not for the :scope pseudo-class, which is still supported. <style scoped> made it possible to explicitly set up element scopes, but ongoing discussions about the design of this feature as well as lack of other implementations resulted in the decision to remove it.

name: button:hover
description: Matches while a pointing device designates the button. Touch behavior varies; preserve another way to reach essential controls.

name: button:active
description: Matches while the button is being activated, commonly between pointer press and release.

name: input:focus
description: Matches the input currently holding focus, including pointer or keyboard focus.

name: button:focus-visible
description: Matches a focused button when the browser decides a visible focus indicator is appropriate, often during keyboard navigation.

support.notes: Alternative name :-moz-focusring (since 4).

name: .field:focus-within
description: Matches a field when it or a descendant has focus. Useful for styling a wrapper around a focused control.

name: a:link
description: Matches hyperlinks whose target has not been visited.

name: a:visited
description: Matches visited hyperlinks. Browsers restrict the properties and information available to protect browsing history.

name: a:any-link
description: Matches an anchor that is a hyperlink, whether its target is visited or unvisited.

name: :target
description: Matches the element identified by the URL fragment, such as the section addressed by #pricing.

name: input:checked

name: input:enabled
description: Matches controls that are enabled under their HTML semantics.

name: input:required
description: Matches form controls with a required value constraint.

name: input:optional
description: Matches eligible form controls that do not require a value.

name: input:valid
description: Matches controls whose value satisfies applicable validation constraints.

name: input:invalid
description: Matches controls whose value fails applicable validation constraints. An empty required input can match immediately.

name: input:user-invalid
description: Matches an invalid control after the browser determines the user has interacted enough to show validation feedback.

support.notes: Alternative name :-moz-ui-invalid (since 4).

name: input:placeholder-shown
description: Matches an input while its placeholder text is displayed.

support.notes: Alternative name :-moz-placeholder (since 4). Support from 4 removed in 51.

name: input:indeterminate
description: Matches a control in an indeterminate state, such as a checkbox whose indeterminate property is true.

name: .label::before
description: Creates a generated pseudo-element before an element’s contents. A non-none content value is normally needed to render it.

support.notes: Alternative name :before (since 1).

Before Firefox 57, Firefox had a bug where ::before pseudo-elements were still generated, even if the content property value were set to normal or none. Before Firefox 3.5, only the CSS level 2 behavior of :before was supported, which disallowed position, float, list-style-* and some display properties. Alternative name :before (since 1).

name: .label::after
